title: Latency-aware billing adjustments for streaming peak events
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Hypothesis: Introducing temporary, latency-aware billing adjustments (credits or reduced outbound token rates) during verified stream peak events will reduce churn for latency-sensitive customers and improve retention without materially increasing unit cost for Redwood. This experiment targets Hosted API streaming sessions that exceed a configurable 95th/99th latency threshold across a sustained window. The adjustment is intended as a customer-level credit (billing adjustment) and a routing incentive for customers to accept best-effort fallbacks during peaks.

Design overview:
- Detect peak: server-side detection of streaming peak windows when 95th latency > X ms for > Y minutes for a region/model.
- Qualify customers: customers with SLA tier >= "Standard" and active within last 30d qualify.
- Adjustment types (A/B test):
  A) Temporary output-token discount (reduce egress rate by 25% for affected tokens during the peak window).
  B) Billing credit equal to estimated extra latency cost (flat per-session credit) applied next invoice.
  C) Control: no billing change; only best-effort routing and a notification.
- Measurement: retention lift over 90d, ticket volume change, net unit economics delta, abuse/fraud signals.

Why different from prior IO experiments: prior docs focused on asymmetric ingress/egress ladders and minimums; this experiment ties billing behavior directly to operational latency events and aims to be protective for customers during transient infra constraints rather than changing baseline IO pricing.

Constraints: must coordinate with billing, invoicing pipeline, and legal. Need safe-guards to prevent gaming (rate limits, session continuity checks).
decision_rationale: We selected a credit-first approach for one arm (B) and a discounted egress arm (A) to see which is clearer to customers and simpler operationally. Discounting egress in-flight has higher operational complexity (metering and retroactive token attribution) but is more immediately visible on usage dashboards. Credits are simpler to apply but may be perceived as 'after the fact' and less satisfactory. The A/B design lets us measure both. Control arm required to gauge natural churn during peaks.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Marco Ruiz: Kickoff w/ billing and infra. ENG flagged potential complexity in retroactive per-token discounting; suggested session-level crediting as fallback.
2026-02-20 - Sasha Nguyen (Billing): Drafted credit application flow and invoice metadata tags. Linked PR for invoice UI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4123

2026-03-02 - Design review (Sandra Kim): UX for customer notification modal and dashboard card approved with minor copy edits; Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIC/Latency+Aware+Billing

2026-03-05 - ENG update (Luc Tran): Detection rule prototype in metrics pipeline ready; synthetic replay shows false-positive rate of ~1.1% on short spikes. We recommend requiring 3-minute sustained window to reduce noise.

2026-03-10 - Legal (Priya Rao): Contract/enterprise questionnaire notes: any automated crediting must be surfaced in monthly statement and accepted by finance; flagged one enterprise that requires pre-approved credit logic - adding opt-out flag for certain customers.

next_steps: Finalize infra gating logic with ENG and reduce false positives: adopt 3-minute sustained window and require X requests/min baseline.
Finish billing pipeline changes: implement session-level credit application and invoice metadata tagging (Billing PR linked).
Add enterprise opt-out flag and notify sales of impacted customers for pre-approval per legal request.
Create experiment runbook and on-call escalation steps for potential abuse/gaming during rollout.
Schedule 2-week pilot rollout to 10% qualifying customers on 2026-03-20 and observe for 30 days; collect retention and NPS delta.
outcomes_criteria: Primary success: 90-day retention for affected customers improves by >= 3 percentage points versus control arm.
Secondary: customer-reported satisfaction (NPS) increases by >= 0.5 points in survey sample.
Unit economics: gross margin impact < 0.5% across pilot cohort or offset by decreased churn within 180 days.
Operational: false-positive detection rate < 0.5% after gating rules; zero billing disputes from pilot enterprises requiring manual intervention.
rollback_plan: Automated disable: if billing disputes > 2 for a given 24h window or if abuse signals (high token replays tied to crediting) detected, disable experiment for all affected customers and revert billing changes. Finance will apply manual reversions where needed and inform customers. Engineering will disable detection-triggered crediting flag immediately.
notes_from_research: Interviewed 7 enterprise customers about perceived value of credits during latency events. Common themes: customers prefer proactive mitigation (routing/fallback) plus transparent crediting. Some prefer immediate discounts to usage billing; others value a consolidated invoice credit. Suggested clear dashboard callout in product.
